new_statements.quote: El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). Es invariable en el proceso de derivación. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce función distintiva. [...] [p.56] De acuerdo al informe de la Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel, además de registrar el acento fijo (agudo o último) también se registra los patrones de acentuación: acento penúltimo y acento en sílaba pesada, que ocurren en muy pocas palabras y en algunas variantes.
new_statements.translation: The accentuation pattern in all variants of the Kaqchikel language is fixed; its function is demarcative and its position is on the final syllable (acute, i.e. last-syllable, stress). It is invariant under derivation. Therefore it need not be written, because it is predictable and has no distinctive function. [...] According to the report of the Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel, besides the fixed (final) stress, the following stress patterns are also recorded: penultimate stress and stress on a heavy syllable, which occur in very few words and in some variants.
new_statements.citation: Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel (Academia de Lenguas Mayas de Guatemala); investigadores/analistas J. E. Ajsivinac Sián, Lolmay P. O. García Mátzar, M. Chacach Cutzal, I. E. Alonzo Guaján. 2004. Gramática descriptiva del idioma maya Kaqchikel: Rutzijoxik rucholik ri Kaqchikel ch'ab'äl. Chimaltenango: CLK-ALMG.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened the held page renders of CLK-ALMG 2004 'Gramática descriptiva del idioma maya Kaqchikel' at (printed p.55), -p.56), -p.57) and the credits page. Printed p.55, section '. /. Acento', third paragraph reads exactly: 'El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). Es invariable en el proceso de derivación. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce función distintiva.' followed by 'A continuación se subrayan las sílabas donde hay acento' and a list with final syllables underlined (nupatz'an, patän, kumätz, tukur, qitzij, poqolaj..). Printed p.56,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed and non-contrastive on the last syllable of the word (including derived and compound words; per OKMA 1997 p.20 directional enclitics after verbs/statives take the stress), in every Kaqchikel variety surveyed; a closed handful of native disyllables and nativised Spanish loans have penultimate stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in either grammar.
new_statements.exceptions: Penultimate stress in a few native words (vakix 'cow', tukur 'owl', tata 'señor', nana 'señora', b'alam 'jaguar', anxa 'garlic', janila 'much') and in Spanish loans that are graves (anma, paxa, alb'ertix, xalma); most variants syncopate vakix/tukur/nana/tata to wakx/tukr/nan/tat. A marginal 'heavy-syllable stress' pattern (first vowel + glottal stop in certain transitive verb forms, e.g. xka'rutz'ot; ie/uo diphthongs in loans) in very few words in Santa María de Jesús, Antigua Guatemala, Parramos, San Bartolomé Milpas Altas, Magdalena Milpas Altas and Alotenango (pp.56-57). OKMA 1997 p.21 adds Tecpán b'ala (< b'alam) with penultimate stress and notes loans keep Spanish grave/esdrújula stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the word ('palabra' radical, derivada o compuesta); OKMA 1997 p.20 extends it to compounds of two separate words and to verb/stative + directional enclitic groups, where stress falls on the enclitic. Statement is language-level Kaqchikel, explicitly 'en todas las variantes'; the grammar's dialect data include Santo Domingo Xenacoj. Examples are citation forms with the stressed syllable underlined (nupatz'an, patän, kumätz, tukur, qitzij, poqolaj..).
new_statements.identity_note: kaqc1278 is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry for the retired Ethnologue/ISO dialect code [ckj] 'Santo Domingo Xenacoj Cakchiquel' (Sacatepéquez dept., W of Guatemala City), merged into Kaqchikel [cak] = kaqc1270 in 2009 (ISO CR 2008-053). No Xenacoj-specific phonological description exists (Glottolog 0 refs; Ethnologue 15 lists only three SIL vernacular literacy booklets). The quoted statement is language-level Kaqchikel from the ALMG Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel descriptive grammar, which draws on the CLK dialect-variation survey whose municipalities include Santo Domingo Xenacoj (pp. 43, 56, 120) and which asserts the final-stress rule 'en todas las variantes'. The only dialect-restricted deviation it reports ('acento en sílaba pesada') is confined to Santa María de Jesús, Antigua, Parramos, San Bartolomé Milpas Altas and Magdalena Milpas Altas, i.e. not Xenacoj. The catalog entry, if made, should be flagged as inherited from the cak/kaqc1270 language-level description.

new_statements.quote: [sec. 2.1.1] The forms in (5) show that [ʔ]-insertion is conditioned only by the initial segment of the word, and not by syllable count or stress (which is almost always word-final in Kaqchikel). [sec. 3.2] In particular, the domain of stress in Kaqchikel is the prosodic word, but high-attaching prefixes are uniformly unstressed (stress is basically restricted to word-final position in Kaqchikel; see Bennett 2016 and references there). [fn. 7] Secondary stress has never been reported for Kaqchikel [...] it seems safest to assume that there is no word-level secondary stress at all in Kaqchikel.
new_statements.citation: Bennett, Ryan. 2018. Recursive prosodic words in Kaqchikel (Mayan). Glossa: a journal of general linguistics 3(1): 67.

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the existing ALMG 2004 statement (fixed final, demarcative, all variants): agrees on final stress and adds detail: domain of stress is the prosodic word, prefixes are stressless, compounds may bear one stress per member, no secondary stress, and one uncertain possible exception (absolutive prefixes in non-verbal predicates). No dedicated stress section: the statements occur in the [ʔ]-insertion argument (sec. 2.1.1), the anti-Clitic-Group argument (sec. 3.2) and footnotes 7 and 9. The work describes Kaqchikel at the language level (data from Cojtí Macario et al. 1998, García Matzar et al. 1999, Patal Majzul et al. 2000, Patal Majzul 2007, plus fieldwork; one Comalapa examp…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the final syllable of the prosodic word ('almost always' / 'basically' word-final); prefixes, whether high- or low-attaching, are stressless; the stress domain is the prosodic word, so compounds can carry a final stress on each member (ex. 26: b'anöy ch'akät [ɓ̥a.ˈnɔj̥ # t͡ʃʔa.ˈkət], meqeb'äl ya' [me.qe.ˈɓ̥əl̥ # ˈjaʔ]), while some root compounds have a single final stress; lax vowels and [ʔC] clusters are confined to stressed word-final syllables and serve as diagnostics of stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Explicitly denied: 'no positive phonotactic evidence for secondary stress in Kaqchikel', 'safest to assume that there is no word-level secondary stress at all' (fn. 7).
new_statements.exceptions: Hedged as 'almost always' / 'basically' word-final without listing exceptions (refers to Bennett 2016 for non-final cases). Fn. 9: absolutive markers in non-verbal predicates are sometimes transcribed with a lax vowel (öj winaqi' 'we are people', Patal Majzul 2007: 50), which would make them stress-bearing prosodic words, but sources disagree on the transcription and they 'do not sound stressed to my ears'.
new_statements.identity_note: kaqc1278 is a Bookkeeping glottocode (retired ISO ckj, merged into Kaqchikel cak in 2009). Bennett 2018 is a language-level description of Kaqchikel drawing on grammars and dictionaries by native-speaker linguists (Cojtí Macario et al. 1998; García Matzar et al. 1999 [PLFM, Antigua]; Patal Majzul et al. 2000 [dialect variation]; Patal Majzul 2007 [dictionary]) confirmed by fieldwork; one example is labelled Comalapa Kaqchikel. It says nothing specific to the Santo Domingo Xenacoj variety. The final-stress statement is therefore Kaqchikel-wide; it applies to Xenacoj only via ALMG 2004's claim that the rule holds 'en todas las variantes' (whose dialect survey included Xenacoj).

sources.citation: Nelson, Brett C. 2020. Right-edge phonological phenomena in Kaqchikel. Calgary Working Papers in Linguistics 31: 72ff.
sources.note: Abstract/intro (read): prosodic structure 'primarily stress-final'; quotes Brown, Maxwell & Little (2006) that 'word stress in Kaqchikel is generally on the final syllable of a word'; tense-lax contrast surfaces only in stressed (word-final) syllables. Fieldwork around Antigua (Sacatepéquez).

sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan & Robert Henderson. 2018 (ms.). Nasal hardening and aspect allomorphy in Kaqchikel. UC Santa Cruz / University of Arizona (author PDF).
sources.note: sec. 3.1 (Comalapa Kaqchikel): 'Stress in Kaqchikel is quite uniform, falling mostly on word-final syllables, with only a very small handful of exceptions showing non-final stress of any kind'; tense/lax vowel contrast licensed only in stressed (final) syllables; 'with few exceptions, stress is word-final' in Tz'utujil, Kaqchikel and related K'ichean languages.

sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan. 2016. Mayan phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 10(10):469-514. doi:10.1111/lnc3.12148 (author PDF, people.ucsc.edu/~rbennett)
sources.note: sec. 6.1 p.495: final stress is the norm in K'ichean; 'Kaqchikel, for instance, follows the typical K'ichean pattern of final stress, but non-final stress occurs in both loanwords (anima [ˈʔanima] 'spirit') and in some native words (janila [χanˈila] 'very').' sec. 6.1.2: Berinstein 1979 found pitch, amplitude and duration cue stress in Kaqchikel.

sources.note: pp.20-21 (Fonología, 'Acento'): 'El Kaqchikel se caracteriza por tener acento fijo en una sílaba determinada. El acento es agudo, lo que significa que la acentuación siempre va a recaer en la sílaba final de la palabra (radical, derivada o compuesta por dos raíces unidas o dos palabras separadas). Al agregar enclíticos a los verbos y estativos (como direccionales), el acento tiende a caer sobre éstos.'
